question: PLAN-V2-PRODUCT §G nominates Apple's engagement metrics — retention, sessions, active devices, deletions — as the guardrail that decides whether to stop a monetization rollout. On 2026-08-26 none of those reports existed. This checks again, and calibrates what arrived against the Sales and Trends census.
myEarlierClaimWasWrong: On 2026-08-26 I recorded that the engagement reports 'should be planned as permanently unavailable at this traffic level', reasoning from the fact that 8 of 156 reports had arrived and every one was acquisition-side. Both Codex and Gemini 3.7 Flash independently flagged 'probably never' as an inference rather than a measurement. They were right, and re-checking on 2026-08-30 falsified it: App Sessions Standard and App Store Installation and Deletion Standard have both materialised.

sessions.note: the Counts column sums to zero — session volumes are suppressed at this scale

whatThisSettles: The honest statement is neither 'they will never come' (my inference, now falsified) nor '28 hours is just pipeline lag' (true, and incomplete). It is: THEY COME, AND THEY CANNOT CARRY A GUARDRAIL. One deletion event and zero session counts cannot answer 'did monetization damage use'. §G's rollout guardrail is unavailable in practice, and the reason is sample size rather than absence — which is a reason that only shrinks as traffic grows, so it is worth re-checking, not worth planning around.
consequenceForStage1: Both Codex and Gemini, asked independently, chose shape B — ship the tip jar with NO transmitted telemetry and keep Data Not Collected — and both argued it from statistical power rather than from privacy: at ~72 downloads/month no telemetry could detect a retention change either. This measurement replaces that argument with a number: Apple's own sample is 9.2% of a 109-install base.
ownedElsewhere: docs/measurements/v2-stage0-baseline.md and PLAN-V2-PRODUCT.md §G still carry the 'plan for permanently unavailable' wording. Both belong to the peer session under the working split; it has been told.
